A natural contrarian though I may be, I have to be a genuine hater here, I did not enjoy Snatch . I'm not intimately acquainted with the genre - or the culture these films aim to 'replicate' - but this feels like parody, and not in a particularly entertaining way. While there is some semblance of stylism in the editing, the majority of these instances range from boring to tacky. The burning caravan scene is cool, and I like the POV shots of characters lying on the ground with others literally looming over them, but it’s too overused to be effective. They try to mix it up with Dutch angles to the same end, but it doesn't work for me. Powerpoint transitions, GTA split screens and rotating jpegs, I know we're living it up in the year 2000, but this looks so cheap in modern viewing. The colours are washed out to emulate a sort of grittiness but the grimmer moments just fall flat for me in the direction. The music is weirdly jaunty at moments where it doesn't quite gel with what's happening (put a pin in that) and Errol & Tony are the only marginally intimidating performances, everyone else feels a bland. Much like a lot of the dialogue, a lot of these performances feel like they’re read directly off the page. Oh man the dialogue draaaaaags. Every time Sol, Vincent and Tyrone are on screen I'm begging for them to just get on with it, every conversation feels like: The car crashes, "you just crashed the car," "why did you do that?" "yeah, why did you do that?" "well, I didn't do it on purpose," "yeah, you shouldn't have done that," "yeah" ...Like, if this is parody, I'm sure it's brilliant, but fuck me, maybe I'm too brain-rotted by instagram reels and better action films, I'm so bored, I do not care. There are some moments that tap into the inherent poetry of the cockney dialect, my favourite being 'as bent as the Soviet sickle, and as hard as the hammer that crosses it' but the majority borders on cringe. The pacing is so slow, yet whenever something interesting happens, it's over before it's even started. Anticlimactic first boxing match, anticlimactic bookie heist, anticlimactic gun shots to the head, I have no idea what we're working towards here. It feels like the same scene over and over again in pursuit of a 86-carat Macguffin. Jason Statham narrates intermittently but it's unclear why he is the POV character for the majority of this film. When the diamond conveniently happens to him at the very end, there is slight satisfaction of things coming together, but it doesn't feel particularly clever or meaningful. I wouldn't mind if there was some other sort of interesting spectacle happening at any point, but there's nothing here. The final boxing match is slightly better than any of the action pieces before it, but it's not a scratch on the Sherlock Holmes (2009) boxing match, also directed by Guy Ritchie, which is disappointing. An... interesting role for Brad Pitt...everyone saying Pitt is incomprehensible is crazy, I easily understand it, or maybe I'm just someone who is northern and actually interacts with people outside of my dialect. It always bothers me when they get A-Listers to play poor people with their perfect Hollywood teeth, though of course Pitt's performance isn't the only elephant-sized/shaped issue with the framing of the traveller community in this film. Take a shot for every racial slur - if you thought The Gentleman was bad, Snatch will give you a stroke. The Jewish stereotyping is also pretty egregious. Musically, there's this grotesquely hokey Yiddish scoring whenever a Jewish person in on screen, though arguably it specifically appears only when 'fake Jews' are on screen, i.e., The Head and the costumed thieves in the opening. If we're being charitable, this sonic stereotyping could be an exercise in satirical hyperrealism to draw attention to the false semitic surface, but I think it's unlikely. From what I understand in his other work that I've heard, John Murphy ranges from competent but boring in James Gunn's Superman (2025), to the brilliance of 28 days later , so this could swing either way. Messy, directionless, dull, and confusing in tone - this one just wasn't for me.

O filme é uma mistura de queime depois de ler com os infiltrados, só que ruim. Mais um filme daqueles que parece que só existem homem cis no mundo. O filme tenta se construir em cima do absurdo, mas faz isso super mal. A cinematografia tenta inovar na linguagem do cinema, com cortes rápidos com cenas ilustrativas das situações tipo em requiem for a dream, mas o timmimg dos cortes é péssimo. O que torna o filme pior é que ele tenta ser bom e no fim é muito ruim. Duas estrelas só pq o absurdo de algumas cenas tira uma risadinha ou outra, mas sugiro não perder seu tempo vendo.

as far as action movies go, this one was about as close to a 12 year old boys fever dream as you can get. It’s two whole hours of complete chaos and i was so confused and lost practically the entire time. It’s like the director said “let’s mash as many tropes as we can into one movie”. You’ve got crime, boxing, killing, gunfights, murder, blackmailing, robberies, heists, and so much more in one single movie and everyone speaks with a heavy indecipherable accent. I figured that was supposed to be funny but because I had no idea which character was which or what was going on, I found it rather irritating. I even paused the movie several times to google the plot summary to decipher what the hell was going on. i mean, why was jason statham’s character the only one who had a narrated inner monologue? Was he supposed to be the main character? I was honestly left with more questions than answers when the credits rolled. overall not my favorite although i can see why others might find parts of it funny
